# THE ROSETTE IN THE ROUND

*The deck with every choice removed: three perfect shells, one still centre,
and the argument that this, and only this, is the true representation of the
twenty-seven.*

## I · THE POINT NOBODY PLACED

Every card is three trits: time, depth, state, each one still, flowing, or
turning. Write stillness as zero, flow as one, turning as minus one, and a
card's code is a set of coordinates. That is not a visualisation laid over
the deck; it is what a card is. Twenty-seven cards, twenty-seven points, the
lattice of three values in three places. The deck has been an arrangement in
space since the day the codes were sealed, whether anyone drew it or not.

## II · THE RADII ARE PYTHAGORAS

How far does a card stand from the centre? Square the coordinates, add, take
the root. A moving layer contributes exactly one; a still layer contributes
nothing. So a card with one, two or three moving clocks stands at exactly
the square root of one, two or three, always, and no hand was involved. The
flat rosette drew those three circles as its compass marks from its first
day. They were never a convention. They were a three-dimensional fact,
quoted by a figure that did not yet know it.

## III · THE THREE PERFECT SHELLS

Sort the twenty-seven onto their three spheres and ask whether they scatter.
They do not. On each sphere the cards stand in perfect even array, and not
in any array: the six one-moving cells are the vertices of a regular
octahedron; the twelve two-moving cells are the vertices of a cuboctahedron;
the eight three-moving cells are the corners of the cube itself. Nothing was
moved to make this so. The frames were measured before they were drawn:
nearest neighbours on each sphere, derived from distance alone, give twelve,
twenty-four and twelve edges, and those counts are pinned by test. The
rosette in the round is the deck wearing this truth: the shells as visible
spheres, each card's knot at its own seat, each shell joined by its own
frame.

## IV · THE OLDEST SENTENCE IN GEOMETRY

Why these three solids? Because the deck's grammar happens to speak the
oldest sentence the geometers know. The octahedron is the cube's dual: swap
faces for corners and each becomes the other. The cuboctahedron is their
reconciliation: shave a cube to the midpoints of its edges, the exact
halfway point of the passage toward its dual, and the cuboctahedron appears.
The sequence cube, rectified cube, birectified cube is a classical object,
and the deck generates all of it from a single instruction, count the moving
clocks, then nests the whole family on three spheres. A cube, its dual
inside it, and their meeting held between them: that is the object.

## V · THE EQUILIBRIUM OF THE TWELVE

One measured fact stands quietest and deepest. The middle shell's radius is
the square root of two, and the distance between its neighbouring cells is
also the square root of two. Radius equal to edge is the defining property
of the cuboctahedron and of no other figure: it is the arrangement of twelve
spheres kissing one, the local law of the densest packing, the shape in
which the push outward and the pull sideways balance exactly. The deck's
twelve, which the calendar's twelve folds already meet on the astrolabe's
ring, stand in that equilibrium around the still centre. The claim here is
the arithmetic and only the arithmetic, which anyone may recompute; the
names other traditions gave this figure stay on the lineage shelf, method
transferring, vocabulary never.

## VI · THE DIAMETERS, AND THE STILL CENTRE

A card's answer is its negation, every trit flipped, and in coordinates
negation is the point reflection through the origin. So every card and its
answer are exact antipodes of the solid, and the diameters the flat rosette
has always drawn are not a diagram convention but true diameters of a body,
silver facing gold across the centre because the outer trit changes sign on
the way through. The Seed, the one card that is its own answer, is the one
point the reflection cannot move: the still centre, dark, the null never
lit. Every law the flat instruments keep turns out to be a property of this
object seen from some window.

::figure rosette-27::

## VII · THE WINDOWS

Each of the family's surfaces is this object through one honest, chosen
window. Look down the long diagonal, the only line of sight that treats the
three clocks alike, and the solid casts the hexagonal shadow whose stacks,
pulled apart by restlessness, are the astrolabe's plate: the flat rosette
borrowed its name from the solid all along. The plate is its flat pose; the
shadow is its projection count; the water is its embedding one dimension up;
the loom is the same body inhabited, with time threading the roads. The
windows differ in what they must hide. The object hides nothing.

## VIII · ZERO FIAT

Ask of any picture of the deck: how many decisions did a hand make? The
plate needs one declared fiat, the seats of the two cards that are invisible
down their own diagonal, and it accepts the even eightfold for calm. The
shadow needs a chosen axis. The water chooses the pole of its projecting
eye. The rosette in the round needs nothing. The seats are the codes; the
radii are Pythagoras; the frames are nearest neighbours, derived; the
spheres are the radii made visible; the diameters are negation; even the
two exiles need no grant here, standing at their own corners like every
other card. It is the only representation of the twenty-seven in which
every element is forced, and that is the exact sense in which it is true:
it could not have been otherwise. Everything else the portal draws is this
object, seen through a window somebody honestly chose.

The object stands in its own room, with nothing else on the bench: a touch
on a glyph names it and the room leans in; a touch on its lit answer flies
the diameter, through the still centre, the involution travelled rather
than stated; a double touch stands back to the whole. One solid at a time
may be brought forward, the others ghosted to context, and the breath
eases the three spheres apart and home again so the nesting is felt as
depth. The room is graduated: the tenth door of the portal's bar, seated
beside the astrolabe at the architect's word. The live surface:
[the rosette](/app/luminara-rosette.html).

## PROVENANCE

*Set down on 11 August 2026, at the architect's word, after the finding of
10 August that reseated the flat rosette by the cube's shadow and the day of
building that followed: the solid held in the hand, the shells dressed, the
plate and shadow and water as its poses, and the loom as the body inhabited.
The shell frames and their counts of twelve, twenty-four and twelve, and the
equality of the middle shell's radius and edge, are pinned in
core/tests/cubeInHand.test.ts; the seats, bisectors and stations of the flat
plate in core/tests/skyWitness.test.ts; the torus roads and the thread's
laws in core/tests/loom.test.ts. The live surfaces are the cube in the hand,
archived whole on the workshop's study shelf, and the loom, on the bench.
Every claim above is coordinate and construction, recomputable by anyone;
nothing here predicts, and nothing here prescribes.*
